ic.in_process_reference: ParallelRho, section 23's and rule v3's own matched rho, three repetitions, median repetition
ic.online_interval: section 23's: the descent's first query to the logarithm checked as [d]G = Q; five exclusive phases
ic.producer: crypto ic price --params <section 23 T<i>.params.json> --json --single-target --rho-seed 0x230000+i, at crypto 995ea207 (IC programme baseline v3, the code rule v3 measured)
ic.recipe: section 23's, unchanged (research/ic_single_target_20260930/runs/k*/T*.params.json at the harness commit)
ic.setup: median over the three repetitions of setup_ns (factor base, collection, linear algebra, descent solver; everything before the target)

strong.config: configs/default_strong.json: fold kernel selection (the one-word Gf2 at n <= 64, as tuned), 32 lanes, DP 4, escape off, step cap factor 2000: the library's default StrongRhoG parameters on the degree's native field

strong_wide.config: configs/default_strong_wide.json: wide, 32 lanes, DP 4, escape off, step cap factor 2000: rA770/rA819's exact configuration (default StrongRhoG<WideGf2,u64>), the two-word field at every n

tuned.config: A's selected_config.json at crypto 770f6a69: fold, 64 lanes, DP 6, escape off, step cap factor 2000 (rT770)
tuned.field_kernel: fold is the Gf2_128 two-word fold kernel, defined only for 64 < n <= 127; at every size here (n <= 61) the worker runs the library's one-word field Gf2 (pclmulqdq with fold reduction where the modulus allows), the walk's own one-word kernel, and records field_type

claims: section 23's claims.py (harness commit, two label edits only) assembles and checks every IC row's vs_rho claim against its in-process rho and replays both certificates in oracle.py; verify_receipt.py builds the same claim with each external rho substituted and runs the same checker (boundary_autolab.validate_claim, stage vs_rho)
class: accounting: no algorithm changes; the reference changes

controls.aa: R2 over R1 for T01-T04, per arm; rho walk steps must be identical between R1 and R2; timing ratios reported

cases.source: rT770 on Q0 at seed 202610061, reconcile run 38617911080
rA770/rA819 on Q0 at seed 202610061, reconcile run 38617911080

controls.identity_rule: each case's walk steps equal the expected count and its scalar the expected scalar; this shows the derived worker is rT770's and rA770's walk
controls.per_row_identity: on every point the IC, ParallelRho, strong, strong_wide and tuned scalars are equal, the IC's regenerated target equals the frozen point, the worker's curve (order, generator) equals the IC fixture's, and each external scalar replays as [d]G = Q in crypto's oracle.py
controls.positive_rule: ln(online_ms positive_hi / positive_lo) within 0.10 of ln(14229982/5353957) = 0.978: the timing instrument resolves an effect of the size under study

estimate: builds 15-30 min; controls about 1 min; panel: section 23's 408 IC processes ran in 73 min at v3 (rule v3), plus 1,632 rho processes at 0.03-3 s each (local smoke at n=41: 30 ms tuned, 126 ms wide default) -> about 1.5-2.5 h; claims and verification 10-20 min. Total about 2-3.5 h of a 6 h job, so the 384 points are kept.
isolation: Tier 1, instance scoped: one fresh GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner, every process pinned to min(sched_getaffinity) with isolated_bench's clean environment and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1; isolated_bench's Tier 1 noise gate (cgroup throttling, steal on the CPU, major faults) per process. A failed or contended attempt is kept and run again up to twice; the first clean valid attempt is the row (section 23's rule). If all three attempts are flagged, the first valid attempt is the row, marked flagged: it stays in the figures, the size reports how many flagged rows it used, and the online ratio is also given without them (claims.py assembles clean rows only).
order: sizes in section 23's order of r; per target, the four arms on that point in ARMS order rotated by (i-1) mod 4 (R1) or i mod 4 (R2); one process at a time on one pinned CPU
question: Ledger section 23's isolated single-target round (crypto research/notes/index-calculus/RESEARCH_IC_BOUNDARY_LEDGER.md section 23; re-run at IC programme baseline v3 as crypto research/ic_tool_program/rule/v3), measured against two external strong-rho references on the same public points: the tuned rho rT770 (fold, 64 lanes, DP 6, escape off) and the default StrongRhoG (32 lanes, DP 4), on the same one-word field kernel as the tuned arm and, as rA770 ran it, on the two-word WideGf2 kernel. Per size: online ratio, cold ratio, break-even and the Bernstein-Lange model, for each reference.

rho_clocks.external: the parent worker's online interval: before the public target's membership and [r]Q subgroup check, through walk starts, walk and collision, to after a generic [d]G = Q replay; curve, normal basis and G-only jumps (preparation_ns_excluded) are excluded and reported as the arm's setup

sources.harness_note: crypto main's current boundary_autolab rejects section 23's claim rows (fields added since); 96911f55, rule v3's results commit, is the latest commit whose checker passed the rule's comparison
sources.toolchain: rustc 1.99.0 (rT770's), installed by rustup in the workflow

statistics.bl_model: Bernstein-Lange (a model, no walk runs): with c the reference's median ms per walk step and P = mean IC setup / c steps of precomputation budget, the online cost is 1.93*1.21*r/(2n*P) steps = 2.3353*r*c^2/(2n*mean IC setup) ms; reported as IC online / BL online
statistics.break_even: mean IC setup / (mean rho online - mean IC online) targets; 'never' if the difference is not positive
statistics.cold_ratio: mean (IC setup + IC online) / mean (rho setup + rho online), same bootstrap
statistics.online_ratio: per size and reference: mean rho online ms / mean IC online ms over the R1 rows (section 23's statistic), 95% paired bootstrap over targets (10,000 resamples, seed 2026101501); median of per-row ratios beside it
statistics.readings: online: 'ic_online_faster' if the interval of rho/IC lies above 1, 'rho_online_faster' if below, else 'not_separated'; cold likewise for IC/rho ('rho_cold_faster' above 1)

targets.aa: T01-T04 again as run R2, every arm
targets.reduction: none: the estimate below fits 384 points in the 6 h job; the time guard skips whole target blocks if it does not, and skipped blocks are reported
targets.source: inputs/targets.json: section 23's T01-T64 public hash-to-curve points (public_hash_seed 23000+i), copied from its committed R1 reports

validity: a size reports figures only if every R1 row of every arm has a valid attempt and every per-row identity holds; otherwise its figures are withheld and the failing rows listed. The round's readings are void if an identity control fails; if the positive control fails they are labelled inconclusive_controls
what_does_not_count: changing sizes, points, seeds, recipes, configs, statistics or rules after any timed row; quoting an online ratio without the cold ratio and the BL model beside it; the BL figure as a measurement; any claim for n=83 or ECC2K-130 from these sizes
